name: MD-05
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+17 partisan lean in the Washington suburbs
Boafo's lopsided money edge: $1.9M raised and $12M+ in outside support versus no visible Republican fundraising
Prediction markets price Democrats near 96 percent
Open seat after Hoyer's retirement removes incumbent advantage but not the district's lean
model.rationale: The district's D+17 lean, Boafo's overwhelming financial advantage, and market pricing near 96 percent all point the same direction, and no polls or opposition spending suggest any narrowing. The open seat adds mild uncertainty but not enough to move this out of the safe Democratic column.
model.watch: A late wave of Republican outside spending or an unexpected development in the open-seat contest could tighten the margin, though the district's lean makes an upset very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Steny Hoyer (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Maryland's 5th District, anchored in Prince George's County and the Washington suburbs, has been a Democratic stronghold for decades, with a partisan lean of roughly 17 points. With Steny Hoyer retiring, Democrat Adrian Boafo enters the general election as the clear favorite. He has raised nearly $1.9 million and drawn more than $12 million in outside support, while Republican Chris Chaffee shows no reported fundraising or outside spending.

Prediction markets put Democratic odds near 96 percent, and no general-election polls exist to suggest otherwise. The district's fundamentals, combined with the lopsided money advantage, point to a comfortable Democratic win in the low-to-mid 20s. The open seat removes the incumbent's personal vote, but the underlying partisan margin is large enough that the race stays firmly in the safe Democratic column.
